text: When you build a REST API, good design matters. First, use clear and simple endpoints, such as /users or /orders, so developers can understand them easily. Second, always return the correct status codes. For example, use 200 for success, 404 when something is not found, and 500 for server errors. Third, write good documentation so others know how to use your API without asking you. Finally, think about versioning. As your API changes, old users may still need the old version, so include something like /v1/ in the URL. These practices make your API easier to use and maintain.
